target.name: Atomic Industries
target.founder: Aaron Slodov, Austin Bishop, Lou Young Jr

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $25M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Atomic Industries is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Aaron Slodov, Austin Bishop, and Lou Young Jr., having raised $25M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 9 comparable companies spanning robotics and adjacent manufacturing automation, including 8 private firms (Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and others) and 1 public benchmark.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $25M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A forward, implies a valuation of $50M. Peer-median analysis leverages four same-sector comparables at Series B and Seed stages—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), Dexterity ($1.6B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B)—yielding a median of $1.7B with a range spanning $1.1B to $2.0B.

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range of $42.5M to $2.0B, with a median of $875M. This dispersion reflects genuine uncertainty inherent in early-stage robotics valuations, where stage-progression conservatism conflicts sharply with peer-based upside assumptions. The peer median assumes Atomic will reach Series B scale and performance parity; the stage-progression figure assumes more modest near-term dilution. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to sampled peers, technical validation progress, and whether robotics/manufacturing subsectors will sustain current public and private multiples.
